_doc: Registry of every repository owned by this account. clone.sh reads this and nothing else — adding a repo here is the only edit needed for it to show up in `./clone.sh --list`, be clonable, and get a symlink. Deliberately NOT submodules: a submodule pins a commit, and this is an index of working clones, not a pinned build input. cloud-master carries a SUBSET of these entries — the cloud project — with identical name/url/private fields; this file is the superset and the two must not disagree.
_self_doc: git-repos-master is the only repo of the account with no entry here. It is the index; an entry would give it a symlink to its own parent directory, which is a loop, not information.
_visibility_doc: `private` mirrors GitHub visibility as of 2026-08-20 and only drives the "(private)" hint in `--list` plus a clearer message when a clone fails for lack of credentials. It grants nothing.
base_dir_doc: Where clones live. Override with $CLOUD_GIT_BASE; otherwise ~/git. Clones are NEVER placed inside this repo — repo_master holds relative symlinks (../../<name> from a group directory) pointing out to them, committed, so `ls <group>/` is the inventory and a dangling link is just a repo you have not cloned yet.
_path_doc: `path` is where the clone actually sits under base_dir; it defaults to `name`. Only the d_lecole entries set it, because those ten were moved into ~/git/lecole-42/ on 2026-08-18 to keep the root of ~/git legible. Indexing them and moving them are separate decisions: `path` lets this file describe where they are instead of demanding they move back.
_archived_doc: FairEmail and octocode forks were deleted on GitHub on 2026-08-18 — FairEmail was fully reproduced by unix/aa_cloud-mail/patches, octocode was 0 commits ahead of Muvon/octocode. Nothing else has been archived. The ten d_lecole repos were deregistered the same day and are registered again as of 2026-08-20; they were never gone, only unindexed.
_fleet_files_doc:
Files that MUST be byte-identical in every repo that has the module they belong to, and where the one authoritative copy lives. `./clone.sh --sync` copies each `from` (resolved under base_dir) to each `to` in every cloned repo that has the entry's `requires` path. `requires` is the OPT-IN and it is explicit on purpose: the obvious shortcut — 'copy where the destination's parent directory exists' — is wrong for any destination at the repo ROOT, because the root always exists. That rule put .mcp.json into all sixteen repos that have no dotfiles module at all (cloud-notes, cloud-u-linux, every lecole-42 entry) on its first run. `requires` names the directory that proves the module is present, so a root-level file is gated by the module it belongs to rather than by its own location.

This exists because 'one shared implementation, many callers' was only ever true by hand. It was not: deploy-dotfiles.sh had already drifted in cloud-infra-desktop (missing the whole claude-SoT refresh block) and was MISSING outright in four repos whose build.sh calls it, and .mcp.json's own _doc admitted 'propagated by hand — nothing automates that hop', which is how cloud-vault ended up without the cloud-infra-mcp headersHelper while cloud had it. Every one of those was a file claiming, in its own header, to be the same file as another.

ADDING a file here is the whole registration: no code change. `from` is <repo>/<path> under base_dir; a `to` list means one source lands at several destinations (mcp.json is both the dotfiles-module source AND the deployed root file, so a repo is consistent whether or not its build.sh has run).

fleet_files.doc: GENERATED by cloud-infra 1_cloud-configs/src/derive/derive-mcp-json.ts from the .mcp blocks in a_solutions/*/build.json. Regenerate there (./9_others/build.sh dotfiles in cloud-infra does it), then --sync to spread it. Only cloud-infra HAS 1_cloud-configs, which is exactly why the other twelve repos could never refresh themselves.

Project-scoped Claude Code settings. Ultimate SoT is da_my-ai/data/claude/settings.project.json; cloud-infra's copy is refreshed from it by deploy-dotfiles.sh, and cloud-infra is the `from` here because it is the only repo whose build reliably runs that refresh. This file gates which MCP servers are dialed at all (disabledMcpjsonServers), so drift here is invisible: a server disabled by a stale copy appears in NEITHER the connected nor the failed list, and reads as missing rather than off.
The headersHelper .mcp.json points at. Must travel WITH the .mcp.json that references it — a repo whose mcp.json names a helper it does not ship gets a silent {} and an unexplained 403.

THE shared dotfiles deploy implementation. Every repo's 9_others/build.sh calls `sh $SCRIPT_DIR/src/deploy-dotfiles.sh` — including four that did not ship the file at all, so their dotfiles verb failed. cloud-infra is the source because it is the only repo whose copy is exercised end-to-end (it alone runs the derive refresh path inside it).

groups.2_vault: Secrets (sops/age) — every credential the fleet uses. Numbered so it sorts ahead of the lettered groups: it is the one repo whose absence breaks the others.
groups.a_cloud: The cloud project — infrastructure, services, data, devices and the tooling built for them. Its own project master is `cloud`, which indexes this same set minus the account-level repos.
groups.b_front: The front-end — the published site, its content, its assets and its experiments. Its project master is `ffront`. Kept out of a_cloud because it ships on its own cadence to its own hosts; folding it in was what made a_cloud mean nothing.
groups.c_gh: Account-level GitHub repos — things that exist because GitHub requires a repo for them, not because they are a project.
groups.d_lecole: 42 / l'École coursework and its experiments. Clones live under ~/git/lecole-42/ (see _path_doc), so these entries carry `path`.
